newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel expects 3 bln shekels from bank offerings.
newsitem.headline: Israel expects 3 bln shekels from bank offerings.

text.p: The Israeli government expects to raise three billion shekels ($890 million) from the sale of bank shares this year, the Treasury's accountant-general, Shai Talmon, said on Sunday.
"It is reasonable to expect the government will raise three billion shekels," Talmon told a news conference.

The government plans to offer 17 percent of Israel Discount Bank on the Tel Aviv bourse in April. It will hold a public offering for 10 percent of Bank Leumi soon after the Jewish holiday of Passover, which falls in late April.
Talmon said the government is considering marketing part of the Leumi offering to foreign investors.
In the second or third quarter of 1997 the government will float at least 20 percent of United Mizrahi Bank on the bourse. Mizrahi is the only major Israeli bank currently not traded.
The government is also accepting offers for a controlling stake of at least 25 percent in Bank Hapoalim, the country's largest bank. The deadline for submitting bids is in mid-April.
Talmon said he expected the sale of the Hapoalim shares would be finalised by July.
The government expects to raise another 400 million to 500 million shekels in dividends from the banks from their divestiture of non-banking assets as required under banking reform, Talmon.
